hook: The Iron Chancellor, who united Germany with "blood and iron".

pages.x: Otto von Bismarck was born in 1815 on his family's estate at Schönhausen, in Prussia. At university in Göttingen he drank, ran up debts and fought duel after duel, and was known as the mad Junker, a wild young country noble.

In 1862 King Wilhelm I made him head of the Prussian government. In his first speech he said the great questions of the day would be settled "not by speeches and majority votes, but by iron and blood."
He fought three short wars: against Denmark in 1864, Austria in 1866 and France in 1870. The victory over Austria at Königgrätz left Prussia the leader of the German states.

In 1870 the king sent him a telegram about a polite meeting with the French ambassador. Bismarck cut it so that it sounded like an insult, and gave it to the newspapers. France declared war, just as he had hoped.
After the French were crushed, the German states united. On 18 January 1871, in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, Wilhelm was proclaimed German Emperor, and Bismarck became the first chancellor.
Now he wanted peace. He wove a web of alliances to keep France isolated, and in 1878 hosted the Congress of Berlin, where the great powers settled their quarrels in the Balkans.
To win workers away from the socialists, in the 1880s he created the world's first national health insurance, accident insurance and old age pensions. Countries everywhere later copied them.

In 1890 the young new emperor, Wilhelm II, forced him to resign; a British cartoon showed it as the pilot leaving the ship. He is said to have predicted that a great war would come out of "some damned foolish thing in the Balkans". He died in 1898.
Bismarck united Germany and made it the strongest power in Europe, and his social insurance laws became the model for the welfare state.
pts: First chancellor of the German Empire
Created the first national health insurance and pensions
